title: Rigveda 5.8: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.8: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.8 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 326v-327r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.8.1-2 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 8, varga 26); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 326v
translation.original_text:
1tvām a̍gna ṛtā̱yava̱ḥ sam ī̍dhire pra̱tnam pra̱tnāsa̍ ū̱taye̍ sahaskṛta | pu̱ru̱śca̱ndraṁ ya̍ja̱taṁ vi̱śvadhā̍yasa̱ṁ damū̍nasaṁ gṛ̱hapa̍ti̱ṁ vare̍ṇyam ||
2tvām a̍gne̱ ati̍thim pū̱rvyaṁ viśa̍ḥ śo̱ciṣke̍śaṁ gṛ̱hapa̍ti̱ṁ ni ṣe̍dire | bṛ̱hatke̍tum puru̱rūpa̍ṁ dhana̱spṛta̍ṁ su̱śarmā̍ṇa̱ṁ svava̍saṁ jara̱dviṣa̍m ||
translation.text:
1O AGNI urged to strength, the men of old who loved the Law enkindled thee, the Ancient, for their aid, Thee very bright, and holy, nourisher of all, most excellent, the Friend and Master of the home.
2Thee, Agni, men have stablished as their guest of old, as Master of the household, thee, with hair of flame; High-bannered, multiform, distributer of wealth, kind helper, good protector, drier of the floods.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 326v (numbered 135v by the scribe) (OPenn image 327, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.7.9 ‹ā yaḥ te sarpiḥ-āsute›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 327r (numbered 136r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.8.3 ‹-santam su-bhaga viśva-darśatam tuvi-svaṇasam›. Verses 5.8.1-2 end on this page.

2tvām | agne | atithim | pūrvyam | viśaḥ | śociḥ-keśam | gṛha-patim | ni | sedire | bṛhat-ketum | puru-rūpam | dhana-spṛtam | su-śarmāṇam | su-avasam | jarat-viṣam

translation.original_ref: RV 5.8.3-7 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 8, varga 26); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 327r
translation.original_text:
3tvām a̍gne̱ mānu̍ṣīr īḻate̱ viśo̍ hotrā̱vida̱ṁ vivi̍ciṁ ratna̱dhāta̍mam | guhā̱ santa̍ṁ subhaga vi̱śvada̍rśataṁ tuviṣva̱ṇasa̍ṁ su̱yaja̍ṁ ghṛta̱śriya̍m ||
4tvām a̍gne dharṇa̱siṁ vi̱śvadhā̍ va̱yaṁ gī̱rbhir gṛ̱ṇanto̱ nama̱sopa̍ sedima | sa no̍ juṣasva samidhā̱no a̍ṅgiro de̱vo marta̍sya ya̱śasā̍ sudī̱tibhi̍ḥ ||
5tvam a̍gne puru̱rūpo̍ vi̱śe-vi̍śe̱ vayo̍ dadhāsi pra̱tnathā̍ puruṣṭuta | pu̱rūṇy annā̱ saha̍sā̱ vi rā̍jasi̱ tviṣi̱ḥ sā te̍ titviṣā̱ṇasya̱ nādhṛṣe̍ ||
6tvām a̍gne samidhā̱naṁ ya̍viṣṭhya de̱vā dū̱taṁ ca̍krire havya̱vāha̍nam | u̱ru̱jraya̍saṁ ghṛ̱tayo̍ni̱m āhu̍taṁ tve̱ṣaṁ cakṣu̍r dadhire coda̱yanma̍ti ||
7tvām a̍gne pra̱diva̱ āhu̍taṁ ghṛ̱taiḥ su̍mnā̱yava̍ḥ suṣa̱midhā̱ sam ī̍dhire | sa vā̍vṛdhā̱na oṣa̍dhībhir ukṣi̱to̱3̱̍ 'bhi jrayā̍ṁsi̱ pārthi̍vā̱ vi ti̍ṣṭhase ||
translation.text:
3The tribes of men praise thee, Agni, who knowest well burnt offerings, the Discerner, lavishest of wealth, Dwelling in secret, Blest One! visible to all, loud-roaring, skilled in worship, glorified with oil.
4Ever to thee, O Agni, as exceeding strong have we drawn nigh with songs and reverence singing hymns. So be thou pleased with us, Angiras! as a God enkindled by the noble with man's goodly light.
5Thou, Agni! multiform, God who art lauded much! givest in every house subsistence as of old. Thou rulest by thy might o'er food of many a sort: that light of thine when blazing may not be opposed.
6The Gods, Most Youthful Agni, have made thee, inflamed, the bearer of oblations and the messenger. Thee, widely-reaching, homed in sacred oil, invoked, effulgent, have they made the Eye that stirs the thought.
7Men seeking joy have lit thee worshipped from of old, O Agni, with good fuel and with sacred oil. So thou, bedewed and waxing mighty by the plants, spreadest thyself abroad over the realms of earth.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 327r (numbered 136r by the scribe) (OPenn image 327, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.8.3 ‹-santam su-bhaga viśva-darśatam tuvi-svaṇasam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 328v (numbered 1v by the scribe), begins in RV 5.9.1 ‹tvām agne haviṣmantaḥ devam›. Verses 5.8.3-7 end on this page; 5.8.3 begins on fol. 326v (numbered 135v by the scribe).
